# Verdict: REJECT **Overall Assessment**: The component is a "silent failure." While it functions visually, it is completely invisible to assistive technology and provides no mechanism for keyboard interaction or timing control. It fails the most fundamental requirement of a notification component: ensuring the user is actually notified. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: - **Predicted**: Missing `role="alert"` or `aria-live` (Confirmed: The component is a plain `div`). - **Predicted**: No keyboard dismiss mechanism (Confirmed: No interactive elements present). - **Predicted**: Timing issues/lack of control (Confirmed: Hardcoded 3s timer with no way to extend). - **Predicted**: Missing semantic "type" (Confirmed: No programmatic way to distinguish success/error). --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings (Blocks Access) 1. **Missing ARIA Role for Notifications** - **Evidence**: `BuggyToast.jsx:23` — The component returns a `
` without any ARIA role. - **User Group**: Screen Reader users. - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages) and WAI-ARIA APG (Alert/Status patterns). - **Why this matters**: A screen reader will not announce the appearance of this toast. The user will be completely unaware that a notification has occurred. - **Fix**: Add `role="alert"` (for critical/urgent messages) or `role="status"` (for polite updates). Given the "Expected Behavior" specifies alert priority, `role="alert"` is required. ### Major Findings (Significantly Degrades Experience) 1. **No Keyboard Dismissal Mechanism** - **Evidence**: `BuggyToast.jsx:23-25` — The markup contains only text.
